source: Hu, Peng, Zhao, Qiu, Hung, Peng (2026) Beyond instrumental and substitutive paradigms: machine culture as an emergent phenomenon in LLMs (Task 1, image generation)
finding: Re-opened PDF. In landscape image generation the US model (DALL-E 3) drew more objects and higher horizons than the Chinese model (iRAG-1.0). The paper calls this an inversion of human data.
limits: Two image generators, not matched text LLMs. Closes gap 4: 8.10 and d=1.01 belong to Task 1 (Chinese mean count); horizon d=0.34 is also Task 1.
agent_relevance: LLM 'culture' flips by task and model; do not use one cultural-style number as a framing signal.

source: Hu, Peng, Zhao, Qiu, Hung, Peng (2026) Beyond instrumental and substitutive paradigms: machine culture as an emergent phenomenon in LLMs (Task 2, scene description)
finding: In text description of images the Chinese model gave more objects than the US model. This runs the other way from Task 1.
limits: Generated counts, one run per condition. d=2.42 is very large and probably reflects model-specific description style, not culture.
agent_relevance: The same model family gives opposite directions across modalities; supports the point that context attention is not a single trait.

source: Hu, Peng, Zhao, Qiu, Hung, Peng (2026) Beyond instrumental and substitutive paradigms: machine culture as an emergent phenomenon in LLMs (Tasks 3-4, attribution and categorization)
finding: Chinese model scored higher on both collective and individual attribution (humans trade these off). In categorization the US model preferred relational pairing more than the Chinese model.
numbers: Collective attribution 3.17 (SD .38) vs 2.81 (SD .25), t=11.35, d=1.14. Individual 4.75 vs 4.67, t=2.70, p=.007, d=0.27. Categorization R-C score: US M=8.10 (SD 1.44) vs Chinese M=6.04 (SD 1.54), t=-13.81, d=1.38, CI [-2.34,-1.78].
limits: Closes gap 4 for the US categorization score: 8.10 is real here, so the repeat of 8.10 in earlier notes is coincidence across tasks, not a copy error.
agent_relevance: A triad task is not a stable probe of a model's framing preference.

source: Hu, Peng, Zhao, Qiu, Hung, Peng (2026) Beyond instrumental and substitutive paradigms: machine culture as an emergent phenomenon in LLMs (Task 6 and statistics)
finding: A third 8.10 in the paper is a t statistic (Task 6, big smiles seen as ideal). So 8.10 appears as Task 1 count, Task 4 score and Task 6 t. All are genuine.
numbers: Task 6: Chinese 0.78 vs US 0.60, t(1553.54)=8.10, p<.001, d=0.40. Task 5 chi-square 28.36 (HAP US 113 vs Chinese 79), 40.91 (LAP 41 vs 2), 7.71 (HAN US 25 vs Chinese 9).
limits: Authors say results are distributional shifts, not human-like psychology. No prompt-wording replication in the paper.
agent_relevance: Verification note: numeric record of the Hu paper is now confirmed.

source: Lacko, Cenek, Arikan, Dresler, Galang, Stachon, Sasinkova, Tsai, Prosek, Ugwitz, Sasinka (2025) Investigating the geography of thought across 11 countries, J Exp Psychol Gen 154(2):325-346
finding: Preregistered 11-country test with Navon and embedded figures plus reaction-time modelling found cross-country differences that did not follow analytic/holistic theory. No rigidity metastyle was found.
numbers: N=993 university students; Armenia, Australia, Brazil, Bulgaria, Czechia, Germany, Ghana, Philippines, Slovakia, Taiwan, Turkiye; Bayesian 4-parameter shifted Wald and hierarchical LBA models.
quote: differences did not align with predictions from analytic/holistic cognitive style theory
limits: Abstract only read. Students, simple perceptual tasks, East Asia only via Taiwan. Closes gap 6 for the 11-country study (b25).
agent_relevance: Perceptual style does not map onto East-West labels; do not use country labels as a source of framing diversity.

source: Lacko, Prosek, Cenek et al. (2023) Analytic and holistic cognitive style as a set of independent manifests: six measurement instruments, PLoS One 18(6):e0287057
finding: Preregistered Czech validation: rod-and-frame task unreliable and linked to intelligence; embedded and Navon tasks recommended; the self-report AHS had an unsatisfactory factor structure; findings did not fit the two-dimension theory.
numbers: N=392 Czech adults, two waves. Pre-set threshold ICC>.50 for drift parameters was only just exceeded by CFT1, CFT2 and E-CSA-WA; the holistic subtest of E-CSA-WA was slightly below it. Navon similarity matching (CFT3) was most stable.
quote: we cannot recommend using of AHS self-report questionnaire in the research in its current form
limits: Czech sample only; AHS factor structure may differ elsewhere. Closes gap 6 for the Czech study (b26): self-report AHS not recommended as a probe, performance tasks better. Full text read.
agent_relevance: If we score our agent with the AHS, the instrument itself is shaky; prefer task-based probes.

source: Cenek, Tsai, Sasinka (2020) Cultural variations in global and local attention and eye-movement patterns: Czech and Taiwanese students, PLoS One 15(11):e0242501
finding: Compound Figures Test gave no clear difference. Eye tracking showed small differences in the predicted direction: Czechs more fixations on focal objects, Taiwanese longer on background. The two tasks were unrelated.
numbers: 60 Taiwanese and 69 Czech students (53 and 67 analysed for the Navon test). Local RT 2.06 vs 1.02 s, global RT 1.89 vs 0.89 s (Taiwanese vs Czech), which reflects speed rather than style.
limits: Partial support for Chua-type eye results, unlike Evans 2009. Small samples. Gap 5: later work is mixed, not a clean null; no large preregistered eye-tracking replication found.
agent_relevance: Attention-style differences are task-specific and uncorrelated across tasks.

source: Na, Grossmann, Varnum, Karasawa, Cho, Kitayama, Nisbett (2020) Culture and personality revisited, J Pers 88(5):908-924
finding: Authors from the original school accept that cognitive-style measures barely correlate. They argue for stable individual profiles across measures instead of one trait.
numbers: Study 1: 233 Americans and 433 Japanese, negligible correlations among cognitive-style measures. Study 2: 485 Americans and Canadians, retest after one month, 235 retained (48%); profiles stable despite negligible correlation.
limits: Profile stability is at the person level; it does not rescue a single mode switch. Bears on gap 9.
agent_relevance: Treat analytic and holistic as separate manifests to toggle one by one, not one dial.

source: Miller, Chapman, Sheppard (2025) A cross-cultural comparison of change detection in driving and non-driving scenes, Acta Psychol 261:106000
finding: UK vs Malaysian drivers showed no cultural difference in change detection in two studies, while safety relevance strongly changed detection. Authors say earlier culture effects were not consistently replicated.
numbers: Two studies, UK vs Malaysian drivers (N not in abstract).
quote: cross-cultural results from abstract tasks may not generalise to real-world contexts
limits: Abstract only. Goal relevance beat culture. Adds to gap 5 as a 2025 null for the change-blindness line.
agent_relevance: Task goals override style: framing should follow the task, not a cultural label.

source: Magid, Sarkol, Mesoudi (2017) Experimental priming of independent and interdependent activity does not affect culturally variable psychological processes, R Soc Open Sci 4:161025
finding: Two experiments with solitary vs collective tasks found no convincing change in self-construal or analytic-holistic cognition in the predicted direction.
limits: Abstract only. Tests an activity prime, not the Oyserman-Lee method. I found no bias-corrected re-analysis of the Oyserman and Lee meta-analysis; gap 7 stays open.
agent_relevance: Human priming is weak evidence that a short prompt can move reasoning style.

source: Oyserman and Lee (2008) Does culture influence what and how we think? Psychol Bull 134(2):311-342
finding: Meta-analysis of the priming literature: moderate effects for relationality and cognition, small for self-concept and values, robust across priming methods.
numbers: Effect sizes described as moderate and small; exact d not in the abstract. Earlier notes: 104 experiments.
limits: Abstract only. The abstract reports no publication-bias test; PubMed searches found no later bias-corrected re-analysis. Gap 7 open.
agent_relevance: Do not assume prompt priming of style from this meta-analysis.

source: Jurkat, Gruber, Kartner (2021) The effect of verbal priming of visual attention styles in 4- to 9-year-old children, Cognition 212:104681
finding: Verbal primes stressing analytic or holistic processing shifted children's gaze and descriptions, but memory only changed after their own verbal productions.
numbers: Children aged 4 to 9; N not in abstract.
limits: Abstract only. Language as the prime worked for attention and description, which is closer to a prompt than culture priming; recognition effects were limited.
agent_relevance: Verbal framing changes what is described more than what is remembered; expect framing prompts to change surface output first.

source: San Martin, Schug, Maddux (2019) Relational mobility and cultural differences in analytic and holistic thinking, JPSP 116(4):495-518
finding: Six studies: lower relational mobility predicts more holistic attention, mediated by external locus of control; Study 4 manipulated it experimentally. A competing explanation to rice farming.
numbers: Six studies; countries US, Spain, Israel, Nigeria, Morocco and Japan (N not in abstract).
limits: Abstract only. Socioecological alternative, relevant to K07 and to the claim that culture labels are poor proxies.
agent_relevance: Style depends on perceived control and context, so framing choice should depend on situation features.

source: Ayturk et al. (2026) The AHS-R: a holistic thinking measure with expanded theoretical domains, PLoS One 21(7):e0353378
finding: Revised scale splits Midway (compromise) and Contradiction (tolerance) as separate dimensions and drops Perception of Change because it loaded negatively on the general holistic factor.
numbers: Turkish samples: Study 1 N=346, Study 2 N=631; four dimensions Causality, Midway, Contradiction, Attention; 7-point scale collapsed to 4 points by IRT.
limits: Abstract only; one country. Gap 9: the dialectical parts get their own place, and the change-perception part does not fit.
agent_relevance: Handling contradiction (Middle Way) can be implemented and tested apart from context attention.

source: Spencer-Rodgers, Major-Siciliano, Yan, Cortijo, McKenzie, Peng (2026) The Dialectical Self Around the World: meta-analysis of country-level means, PSPB
finding: Meta-analysis of the Dialectical Self Scale shows clear regional clustering, tied to tolerance of contradiction, expectation of change, Buddhism and rice, but only weakly to contemporary self-construals.
numbers: k=139 studies, N=23,629, 28 countries; no historical shift across two decades.
limits: Abstract only; self-report scale and authors close to the theory. Gap 9: the dialectical component is replicated at country level on its own, but never shown to predict reasoning accuracy.
agent_relevance: Dialectical framing is a coherent construct, yet its value for a scaffold's contradiction handling is untested.

source: Santos, Requero, Moreno, Brinol, Petty (2025) Certainty in holistic thinking and responses to contradiction, Br J Soc Psychol 64(1):e12782
finding: Holism scores predicted liking of dialectical proverbs and ambivalence calibration more strongly when people were certain of their holism.
limits: Abstract only. A moderator study on the contradiction component, separate from attention.
agent_relevance: Confidence in a framing may matter as much as the framing; links to calibration.

source: Zhang, Cui, Chen, Wang, Zhang, Wang, Wu, Hu (2025) Stop overvaluing multi-agent debate, arXiv 2502.08788
finding: Five multi-agent debate methods on 9 benchmarks and 4 models mostly failed to beat Chain-of-Thought or Self-Consistency, even with more compute. Model heterogeneity helped; more agents or rounds did not.
numbers: No MAD method had a win rate above 20% against CoT across 36 scenarios (4 models x 9 benchmarks). GPT-4o-mini MMLU: CoT 80.73, SC 82.13, SoM 74.73, Multi-Persona 75.47. Heter-SoM +6.4% over SoM-average, Heter-EoT +8.2%, up to +5.8% over CoT-average. Multi-Persona win rate vs CoT 0%.
quote: MAD often fail to outperform simple single-agent baselines such as Chain-of-Thought and Self-Consistency
limits: Closes the equal-token part of gap 8 (such controls exist and sampling beats debate). Heterogeneity was across models, not cultural personas; no study isolates cultural persona diversity.
agent_relevance: Prefer a second independent sample or a different model over a persona debate; test any framing switch against SC at equal tokens.

source: Smit, Grinsztajn, Duckworth, Barrett, Pretorius (2024) Should we be going MAD? ICML, arXiv 2311.17371
finding: Debate systems do not reliably beat self-consistency or ensembling. Multi-Persona was about 7% worse than other systems in the default setup and its debate step lowered accuracy; prompting a 90% agreement level raised debate performance.
numbers: Datasets include MedQA, PubMedQA, MMLU, CosmosQA, GPQA; Multi-Persona about 7% worse in the default setup.
limits: Angel/devil persona debate differs from a cultural framing design. Supports the need for an equal-token control in gap 8.
agent_relevance: Persona-based multi-view prompts can lower accuracy; measure before using.

source: Zheng, Mishra, Chen, Cheng, Chi, Le, Zhou (2024) Take a step back: evoking reasoning via abstraction, arXiv 2310.06117
finding: An abstraction-first framing (state principles, then solve) raised accuracy on principle-heavy tasks but not on all tasks. It is the closest tested analogue to an analytic (rule/category) framing switch.
numbers: PaLM-2L MMLU Physics 66.4 to 73.2, Chemistry 70.9 to 81.8 (CoT 65.0 and 75.3); GPT-4 Physics 69.4 to 84.5 (CoT 82.9). TimeQA 41.5 to 66.0. MuSiQue 35.5 to 42.6. StrategyQA 82.8 to 82.7 (no gain).
limits: Not labelled analytic/holistic, no holistic counterpart tested, no equal-token control against self-consistency. Partly addresses gaps 1 and 2: gains are task-specific, bigger on rule/principle tasks.
agent_relevance: Use an analytic-first pass on principle tasks, and compare it to SC at equal tokens.
